subject: When to post-stratify and when to analyze separately?

messages.author: 397224dbeee02a09
messages.subject: When to post-stratify and when to analyze separately?
parts:
I'm analyzing songbird point-count data collected in several types of
baldcypress swamp in Louisiana, USA, and I have a data preparation and
analysis question. When I examine the data divided into a large number
of distance groupings, the distributions of detection distances vary by
habitat with evidence of heaping at different distances, so different
distance groupings are probably appropriate for each habitat. It seems
that stratifying or post-stratifying by habitat imposes a single set of
distance groupings and a single truncation distance across all habitats.=20

Should I run the analysis both ways and determine the appropriate method
from the fit statistics?

David M. Fox
227 Renewable Natural Resources Bldg.
Louisiana State University
Baton Rouge, LA 70803
225-578-4224

messages.author: 5140016d70f6ba82
messages.subject: Re: When to post-stratify and when to analyze separately?
parts:
In my opinion, developing a set of intervals because of heaping of
distances caused by rounding should be based on an assessment of that
measurement process and not based on the observed data. If you feel you
must use the observed data I would look at it combined or by observer
and not by habitat. What you are interested in is the best way to bin
the data such that any measurement error is minimized. I can't
understand how that would be a function of habitat.

Obviously, the better solution is to use a more precise measurement of
distance, so you are not stuck with this issue.

--jeff
